# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH N. MENINGITIDIS

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely, antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

Meningococcal disease prophylaxis should be given to close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for advice and assistance.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for a total duration of 7 days.

Therapy:
Preferred:

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) M

Alternative:

Assessment of beta-lactam reaction

Consult Infectious Diseases
